title: Let the DC through
story: A sensor at the far end of a cable is powered by a steady DC current that must flow from node a to ground through the empty slot. The 100 ohm resistor is the cable plus the sensor. Fill the slot with a part that lets all of the DC current through, so that node a sits at (almost) 0 V and about 90 mA flow. At DC nothing is changing, so think about what each part does when di/dt and dv/dt are zero.

goals.label: between 85 and 95 mA flow through R1

hints: An inductor's voltage is L times how fast its current changes. A steady current is not changing.
A capacitor at DC is the opposite: once charged, no current flows through it.
